# PromptBar

> A native macOS menu bar prompt compiler. Copy a half-formed instruction, press a
> shortcut, and get three prompts an AI can actually execute. Enhancement runs
> entirely on Apple's on-device Foundation Models — no account, no network requests.

PromptBar is free and MIT licensed. It requires macOS 26 on Apple silicon with
Apple Intelligence enabled.

## What it does

- Rewrites a rough instruction into three variants that differ by construction, not
  by chance: **Minimal** keeps your wording, **Balanced** adds context as prose, and
  **Structured** emits labelled sections (Objective, Context, Requirements,
  Constraints, Expected output). Each is a separate guided-generation field with its
  own structural contract.
- Never invents context. No fabricated word counts, tones, audiences or deadlines;
  missing details become bracketed placeholders and ambiguous terms keep the user's
  own wording.
- Runs a deterministic local prompt check before the model runs.
- **Instant Enhance** (⇧⌥E) rewrites the clipboard in place with no window, keeping a
  restore point.
- An optional **Compile chip** appears beside text selected in any app. It is off by
  default and is the only feature that requests a permission (Accessibility).
- Optional local history, off until enabled, stored only in the app container with
  retention limits and per-app exclusions.

## Privacy

There is no server, so there is no request to inspect. The pasteboard is read only at
the moment of invocation, never in the background. Password fields and excluded apps
are never read. Nothing is stored or transmitted.

## Limits

The on-device session shares one 4,096-token window between the instructions, the
schema, the input and all three outputs, which puts the practical input ceiling around
4,000 characters. PromptBar warns before the limit and refuses rather than truncating.
